name: WhatsApp Nov fixes
tile_line: Real bugs, low risk. Update the app as usual.
summary: WhatsApp fixed three bugs on 20 Nov 2026. The worst one in practice could reveal your phone's IP address to a scammer who sent a crafted ad-reply message, and WhatsApp says it may have been abused with spam; it was already fixed in 2.26.17.4. The other two need you to tap a message sent from an unofficial app, or an attacker inside Meta's own systems, and Meta says neither was exploited.

status.needs: a WhatsApp account to message you (or, for the Meta AI bug, a position inside Meta's infrastructure)

affected.label: An older WhatsApp app
affected.text: The IP address bug (CVE-2026-23871) is in WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android from 2.20.198.3 up to 2.26.17.4. The order-message bug (CVE-2026-102769) is in WhatsApp for Android before 2.26.35.74; its description names only WhatsApp for Android, but the same record also lists WhatsApp Business for Android from 2.22.3.7 up to 2.26.35.74. The Meta AI bug (CVE-2026-44908) is in WhatsApp for iOS before 2.26.24.72, WhatsApp Business for iOS and WhatsApp for Mac before 2.26.23.72, WhatsApp for Android before 2.26.23.74 and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.23.70.

affected.label: Someone sends you a crafted message
affected.text: IP address bug: a crafted Click to WhatsApp ad-reply message, once shown in a chat, can make your phone fetch media from the attacker's server and so reveal your IP address. Order-message bug: you have to tap a crafted "order details" message sent from an unofficial WhatsApp client; it can delete WhatsApp's own locally stored files, and leak one bit of information about your chat database if you're online when it arrives. The Meta AI bug needs someone positioned inside Meta's infrastructure, and Meta says its public certificate ledger confirms no exploitation.

do.label: Update WhatsApp from the store
do.text: Versions that include all three fixes: WhatsApp for Android 2.26.35.74, WhatsApp for iOS 2.26.24.72, WhatsApp Business for iOS and WhatsApp for Mac 2.26.23.72. For WhatsApp Business for Android, sources conflict: HKCERT gives 2.26.23.70 (the Meta AI fix), but the CVE record for the order-message bug lists Business for Android as affected below 2.26.35.74, so get 2.26.35.74 or later.

do.label: No need to rush beyond that
do.text: Meta rates the bugs 3.5 (Low), 6.8 and 4.8 (Medium). CISA's assessment in the CVE records says no exploitation for all three, while WhatsApp says the IP address bug may have been abused with spam messages; WhatsApp told SecurityWeek it found the bug while disrupting a scam campaign. None of the three is on CISA's list of exploited bugs. HKCERT rates the set Medium risk.

versions_skip: WhatsApp ships only through app stores, which install the newest version; the fixed version for each app is in the steps.
slack: WhatsApp, 20 Nov 2026 (CVE-2026-23871, CVE-2026-102769, CVE-2026-44908): three real but low-risk bugs. An Android ad-reply bug could reveal your IP address to a scammer (Meta: may have been abused with spam; fixed in 2.26.17.4). An order-message SQL injection needs you to tap a message from an unofficial client and can delete WhatsApp's own local files (no exploitation). A Meta AI certificate check needs an attacker inside Meta (no exploitation). Meta rates them 3.5, 6.8 and 4.8; not on CISA KEV. Update through the store: Android 2.26.35.74, iOS 2.26.24.72, Business iOS and Mac 2.26.23.72; Business Android 2.26.35.74 (sources conflict, HKCERT says 2.26.23.70).
